utterances.text: For how long have you lived in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have lived in Prijedor since 1974.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter thinks.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Or 84 rather.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps I will repeat the question. We did not hear that perhaps correctly. When did you start to live in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 1984, and I have been working in Prijedor since 1979.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In 1992 in which division of the police did you work? Unfortunately we have gone down. I will repeat the question. I am sorry, Mr. Prpos, but the communication did not come through to us. In 1992 in which division of the police did you work?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I worked in the police station for traffic security.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When did you start that kind of work at the police station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not find the question very clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When did you commence your work in the police station for traffic security?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From 1979.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter cannot hear him any longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In 1992 what was your rank as an officer in traffic security?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In '92 I was Commander of the militia, the police for traffic safety. At that time I did not have a rank because things were not established that way then. There were only functional insignia, so to speak.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you know Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When did you first meet Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I met him when he came to work in the station where I was Commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What did he come to work as at your station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was a policeman, a Reserve Policeman.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you know if that was part of his mobilization or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you know what work he started when he came to your station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you have records that are kept of the duties of police officers within the traffic security?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I would like you now to look at a book that is Defence Exhibit 66A. If a copy of that can be put before you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I was just going to comment about how well things were going and I wonder whether people looking at this wonder what is going on. Our Rules provide for depositions to be taken by video link, but the Defence requested that testimony be offered to the Tribunal by a video link ----

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: --- for the convenience of witnesses and so that has been arranged. We have been hearing the testimony through that procedure very well. It looks like we are back now. OK. Go ahead Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Mr. Prpos, do you recognise that book as being a copy of a document?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter cannot hear anything. There is no sound whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I will repeat the question. Mr. Prpos, we lost your communication then and I will repeat the question. Do you recognise that copy document that has been put in front of you and, if so, can you tell us what it is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I recognise it. It is the daily log, as it were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It is the daily log for what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For the work of policemen for that particular day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is this a log for a particular division of the police?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I am sorry, but there seem to be interruptions in the tone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I will repeat the question again. Is it a record for a particular division of the Prijedor Police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is for the entire police station and I was its Commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Of which police station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is the police for traffic security, safety on roads.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When did this document first begin? From which date does it start?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Specifically this particular document on 1st June 1990.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter could not hear the year.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So that is before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Would that be 1991?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter also has an interrupted tone now. I cannot understand it.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Just ask him to repeat his answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Could you repeat your answer, please, Mr. Prpos. We are having some interference here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was used before the war also, before 1992. So that is in the police station where I worked.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, it may be we are getting a little too many difficulties for the proceedings to flow smoothly at this stage. I know it is before 1.00 o'clock. I can tell on my headphones it is intermittent.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will stand in recess until 2.30, and then we will continue with the video link. However, as the parties have agreed, if it becomes so difficult then we can use the procedure of depositions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: It is up to you, Mr. Kay. Very good. We will stand in recess until 2.30.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, would you continue, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Mr. Prpos, before the break I was asking you to look at a document marked 66A. Can that be placed in front of you, please? You told us before the break that this book began in 1991. Is it right that the cover of the book is dated 1st June 1991?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If you now turn to the second page in the book, is that page a page that contains the official police stamps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is it headed "Official duty plan" both in Latin script as well as Cyrillic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I would like you to now turn to the page in the book which shows on that page the date of 1st June 1991. Can you see that page?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is this a page showing the duties that took place on that date under the command of the then head of the traffic police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is true. The Deputy Commander is signed, and that is the duty that I performed at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. If you could then turn to the next page which is headed "18th August 1991"? Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Again, is this signed at the foot of the page in the right-hand corner by the then head of the traffic police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was Djenadija Marko, Commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We are looking here at pages that have jumped from 1st June to 18th August 1991. Is it right that these are extracts that have been taken from the original of the book which is held at Prijedor police station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is accurate. These are excerpts from the original.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you confirm that this book that we are looking at in this form has had the names of people blanked over?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is true. There is a number of an order of a certain service and the composition of the patrol and the vehicle which they used during patrol.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was it a condition of this being given to the Defence in this form that these names that were not relevant to the Defence could be blanked over?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is true, because this is data which is not relevant, so the names and surnames of other members of the patrols were blanked over.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Could you turn to the next page and is this dated 30th August 1991?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Friday, 30th August 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Again, is this an example of a page of the book before June 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was signed by Commander Fikret Kadiric.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Could you turn to the next page is it headed 14th June 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Sunday, June 14th 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In the right-hand corner of this page, is that signed by you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is not my signature. It is the signature of the policeman who was in charge of records.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What is the name of that policeman?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Cvijic Zoran.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The page that we are looking at for 14th June 1992 we have on our page three shifts for checkpoint Orlovci, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is right, from 17 to 1500, from 1500 to 2100 hours and from 2100 to 0700.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In the parts of these pages that have been blanked out, are they also the shifts for other checkpoints?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Have those details been blanked over in the copying of this document so that it could be handed to the Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was blanked over with a piece of paper actually so in the photocopying it was deleted so you could only see the numbers of the patrol orders that certain services had.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I would like you to tell us, first of all, whose writing is it on this page where we see "punkt Orlovci" and the part of the names of the officers who would have consisted of that duty?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is the handwriting of policeman Zoran Cvijic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How does this book come to be made up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You saw the beginning that, in principle, it is the Deputy Commander who fills this out, because I was carrying out this duty by myself at that time. After certain repetitions in the service, any policeman could have done it. He would only rewrite the shifts for the next day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is this book with its details of the shift patterns at Orlovci written before the shift takes place at that time on that date or afterwards?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is written out a day before the actual duty takes place, and I wish to say that after that this is typed out on a piece of paper and it is officially verified by the Commander, and it is only after that that this timetable is put on a bulletin board so that the policemen can see who was on duty when.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In the typing out of the piece of paper that is put on the bulletin board, is that a document you would have seen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, because it is only when I verify it that it can be put up on the bulletin boards.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What has happened to the piece of paper, for instance, for this date of 14th June 1992? Are those documents kept?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, these documents have not been preserved, apart from this book.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Who decided which officers would take part in which shift?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When did you make that decision that the shifts would consist of certain officers? Was that before this book was written?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before, because then this book comes in as an auxiliary document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So did you communicate to Zoran Cvijic whom you wanted on each particular shift and the time that each shift would have its duty?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, one can see from here that there is a certain equal rhythm, if you look at the actual distribution. If a person works one day, then he does not work the next two days, for example. So this becomes automatic after a time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Could we now turn to the next page which is headed "15th June 1992"? Is this the writing of Zoran Cvijic on this page?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was it written under your authority?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is the signature in the right-hand corner written by him on your behalf?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We see on the date of 15th June 1992 that the checkpoint Orlovci shift between 1500 to 2100 contained Brdar Miroslav and Cvijic Miroslav. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And a third member of the Unit whose name has been blanked out, can you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That third member of the Unit on that day, was that Dusko Tadic or someone else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was someone else. I am not sure, but it is not Dusko Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Miroslav Brdar and Miroslav Cvijic, do you know how long they had been working at checkpoint Orlovci before this time of 15th June 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I could not say with certainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were they regular policemen or reserve policemen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One can see in the records.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were they regular policemen or reserve?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Reserve policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were they forming their duties as part of their mobilization?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, all reserve policemen were performing their duties under the mobilization which existed earlier, before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can we now turn to the next page of 16th June 1992? Is that the writing again of Zoran Cvijic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Has he signed at the bottom right-hand corner on your behalf?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Looking at this page, it shows that 16th June 1992 had at checkpoint Orlovci between 700 and 1500 hours the shift of Dusko Tadic and Miroslav Brdar and Miroslav Cvijic. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you know if Dusko Tadic had worked as a reserve policeman at Prijedor police station before this date of 16th June?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, he did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you tell us why he was given this duty at checkpoint Orlovci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Within the framework of the mobilization and the needs of the service, on the basis of a timetable, he was chosen to work at that particular checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was it your decision that he work at this checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was my exclusive decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was it your decision that he work with this Unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we turn to the next page of 17th June 1992, again is that page written by Zoran Cvijic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The duties performed by that Unit of Cvijic, Brdar and Tadic, would that have taken place under your direction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We know, as we have been through this book, until the end of July 1992 that, in fact, this information is repeated on virtually every day but at varying times. Are you able to confirm that the book throughout this period was maintained in the same way as you have described so far?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If you could now turn to 19th June 1992, that page is written in Cyrillic script. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Would that have been written by Zoran Cvijic in Cyrillic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Zoran Cvijic wrote it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The signature of you also in Cyrillic, would that have also been written by Zoran Cvijic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, Zoran Cvijic wrote it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You have told us that the pages on this book are prepared before the duty happens, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What would happen if one of the policemen did not turn up for his duty and, therefore, failed to attend? Would this book have been amended in any way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you tell us ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The change would be noted in this timetable.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If one of the policemen failed to attend and someone else took over his duty, would that have been recorded then in some form?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the name of the person who did not come would be crossed over and the presence of the other person would be recorded, because in addition to these assignments there is a place where you have to record the absentees, those on holiday, on sick leave, etc. So if he was not on duty, then his name would figure somewhere else in this timetable.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If you could turn to the page of 13th July 1992, do you see that page, 13th July 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do. It is a Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In the bottom left-hand corner we can see -- 13th July 1992, 13th July 1992 ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 13th? Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In the bottom left-hand corner can you see the figure "7" and "Brdar Miroslav"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you see the figure "8" and "Cvijic Miroslav"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you see the figure "9" and "Tadic Dusko"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Why would those names against those numbers appear down in the bottom left-hand corner rather than on any other part of the page?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because they were off duty on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Would that be recorded by a column headed "slobodni" meaning "free"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, you can see "S-L-O", "Slo", indicated here, just the first three letters. That is the column for "slobodni", "free".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Are you confident that these records have been properly maintained at Prijedor police station to reflect the shifts worked by the policemen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I am confident because there are other records in addition to this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, I will look at some other records in a moment with you, but it is the accuracy of this book that I would like you to comment upon, whether you believe it is accurate or not.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do believe it to be accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I would like to now turn to 2nd August 1992. Again, as with other pages, is that a page written on your behalf by Zoran Cvijic ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: --- and in the right-hand corner signed on your behalf by Zoran Cvijic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Again was this like the other pages, a record compiled under your authority?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Again, does that page show on 2nd August 1992 that Tadic Dusko was free on that date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, under the number 18.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. If we turn now to 3rd August 1992, again was this a page compiled in a similar way on your behalf by Zoran Cvijic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, only in this case he wrote in Latin script.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Looking at this book, are you able to confirm that the record for Dusko Tadic working at checkpoint Orlovci begins on 16th June 1992 and ends on 2nd August 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I would now like you to look at some more documents. The document I want placed before you is headed "D63A". Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do. It is an order list.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you tell us where this document comes from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is from the official records of the police station for traffic security which is kept as a document of permanent value.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you confirm again that the page we are looking at is an extract of the pages for June 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And that it was given to the Defence on the condition that the second names of the people on that page were overwritten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, under those conditions it was given.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I would like you now to look at the entry for Dusko Tadic at No. 45. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you tell us who would have written on this page of the document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was written by Cvijic Zoran.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you tell us what exactly is the job or position of Zoran Cvijic? We have crashed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will repeat my last question again as we have linked up again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Mr. Prpos, I asked you what position or job Zoran Cvijic had at the police station. Can you tell us, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that time he was policeman for materiel and technical means and for keeping of records in the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did he work under your authority alone or under the authorities of any of the other Commanders?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was exclusively under my authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did he work in the same office as you or in a different room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had another office.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How close to your office was that office?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was right next to mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I would like you now to ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was next to mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like you now to look at 16th June 1992 column. Can you confirm that that is the first working day recorded for Dusko Tadic at Prijedor police station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is. There is an indication KS-700, from 7 to 15 hours, eight hours, the number of the order, traffic control and the time spent on duty is indicated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you tell us what KS-700 stands for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "KS" is control of traffic, an indication of the type of duty, and "700" is the number indicated -- indicating the type of service.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So what would "700" indicate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It indicated the number of the order for that type of duty, from the timetable of services.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is that a form of work permit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the final part of the task of a policeman. When he finishes his duty, then he enters it into this table.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Looking at 17th June, we see there the figures next to "KS" of "716". Can you help us with the difference in the number there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If you saw earlier on in the timetable, in addition to the Orlovci checkpoint, there were others, so there is a whole series from the new year until the end of the year for all types of duties performed by the station and that is the difference in this number, from 16th to 17th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So if we looked back at that first book, being the official duty plan, D66A, and looked at 16th June, we would see that the shift of checkpoint Orlovci from 700 hours to 1500 hours had "700" against it; that "700" would also be written on this official schedule, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is right. It means that the schedule is linked to this list.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, where is the 700 on 66A?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If your Honour turns to 16th June ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: --- on the left-hand side of the page next to the word "punkt" is the figure 700.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK, it is off the page on our copy, maybe in the copying. We can check it later.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. If I could just help the Court as part of the exercise, on 17th June 1992 there is the figure 716. Is that on your Honours' copies?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, and that then corresponds with the figure on 17th June in the schedule.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Judge Vohrah has a better copy. We will use his copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Right. [To the witness]: This schedule that we are looking at for June 1992, Mr. Prpos, is it written after the work has taken place on each day or before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These records are filled after the duty has been completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If a particular policeman had not appeared for duty on the time or date that he was supposed to in the official duty plan, would it then not be recorded in this sheet here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, these are the accurate data for the actual time spent on duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: For instance, if on 17th June 1992 Dusko Tadic is in the book, the duty book that we looked at first, as being scheduled to work between the hours of 7 o'clock to 1500 hours, if he failed to attend that shift, would the schedule we are now looking at for 17th June then be blank as showing he did not work on that day for those times?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, if he had not worked on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How accurate is this schedule that we are looking for June 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 100 per cent accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We see on this page that there are further days and hours recorded as worked by Dusko Tadic, but those hours vary. If you look at 18th June we see the figure "10". Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is the total number of hours that Dusko Tadic spent on duty on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we look at the 20 ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From 21 to ----

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we look at 20th June, we see 15 to 21 over the figure 6. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was there any reason why the shift time was shorter on that day of 20th June than it had been for the previous two days of 18th and 19th June?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the only reason was that night began and the checkpoint is far removed from the station and it needed time for the policemen to get there. So the night-shifts were longer and the day-shifts were shorter, and this intermediate shift was even shorter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we look at the next page which is for July 1992 -- can you have D64A put in front of you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not have that document in front of me. Would you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you see the page of the book for July 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I need it for July and this is June.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The document we are producing now, your Honour, is D64A. [To the witness]: Is that document before you now headed "July '92"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Again, is that a list of names including the name of Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Again, was this a document that would have been written by Zoran Cvijic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Would it have been written under your authority?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Looking at this document, we again see the names blanked out. Can you confirm that that was again one of the conditions upon which the Defence were able to receive this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. That was required as a precondition, for the other names, the names of the other policemen, to be blanked out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This page that we are looking at, does it come from a book?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is an excerpt from the schedule.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Again, can you confirm that it is the schedule relating to the traffic police for Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Looking at this page, we can see that again the letters "KS" appear above the hours noted. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is there any reason why we do not have any linking number here which would correspond to the numbers within the official duty plan, the first book we looked at?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is an error, an omission on the part of Cvijic who filled in this document, Zoran Cvijic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Again, could you comment upon the accuracy of this document relating to the records of the hours of duty for Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These records are accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I would like you now to look at another document which is D65A. Can you see this document headed "August '92"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you tell us what this document comes from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is an excerpt from the schedule of the traffic police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Again, is it a document that was compiled by Zoran Cvijic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Would that have been under your authority?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you tell us up to what date it shows Dusko Tadic worked for the traffic police at Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: According to this copy, as far as I can see, it is 3rd August from 7 to 19 hours, a total of 12 hours traffic control.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: At the point of 3rd August, can you confirm that it shows that Dusko Tadic carried out no further duties for the traffic police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When we were looking in the book for the official duty plan, that contained the duties of checkpoint Orlovci. If Dusko Tadic had been working for two days at a security point on the bridge over the River Sana, would that have been in the first book we looked at?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We have got him recorded as working here on this schedule, but in the book that we looked at which showed the shifts for checkpoint Orlovci, would that have been within that book if he had been at a security point on the River Sana on the bridge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it would.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Looking at this document here, on the right-hand side there is a "remarks" column. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can, but the copy is a very poor one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Are you able to tell us, so far as you can, what is written in the "remarks" column against Dusko Tadic's name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If we look at it from the bottom, it is the third blank from the bottom, that on 5th August '92 he was transferred to somewhere else, signed by me, and it was written by Cvijic Zoran.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Would that be accurate as a note relating to the ending of Dusko Tadic's duties within the traffic police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you know if Dusko Tadic after he finished working for the traffic police at Prijedor was then transferred to another division of the Prijedor police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know and I did not enquire because I had other business to attend to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What I would like you to do now is to look at another document. These are documents that have not been exhibited yet, your Honour, but it is one that has been handed to the Prosecution labelled A1.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is this a document that you wish to offer once it has been identified?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. That will be what number?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you see this document which we have called here A1, Mr. Prpos?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is it a document that is headed "August '92"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document as being a copy of another document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know it is a schedule, but it does not belong to the station for traffic security.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you tell us for which station it belongs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not, I am afraid, not with certainty. It probably belongs to one of those he was transferred to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will not take this matter any further then with this particular witness. (To the witness): Thank you very much for that, Mr. Prpos, if that document can now be taken away from in front of you? If another document can be placed in front of you labelled C1, which I tender before the Court, your Honour, as I think it is D75. Can you see this document labelled C1, Mr. Prpos?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you tell us what it is headed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the heading it is stated: "The Reserve Station of Police, list of members of the Reserve Police Force in July '92, unemployed".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: July or June 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: June 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is your signature on this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is it a document that has your name on it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in the signature, Commander of the police, Prpos Djuro, signature and stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you tell us what this document, C1, shows?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is a list of members of the reserve police force who received a salary on the basis of this list. You can see the sum and the signature of the worker or policeman in question, the number, the time when he was engaged, the amount in dinars and his signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If you could look at the page behind it, does it show the same information?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, only this is in a frame, but these are the same data and this is my original signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If you would look at the page behind that, page 3, does it show the same information there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, only this is a list from the accounting service.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document as coming from Prijedor police station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This document belongs to the accounting or finance department, because you see on the basis of these numbers that there are many policemen, and this is a record by the accountancy department of those receiving a salary.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is it a document, however, that comes from Prijedor police station? Is this document held there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This document -- the number is in the heading -- is kept in the accountancy department of the station for public security in Prijedor, and the previous two are in the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Are you aware if these three documents were given to the Defence at Prijedor police station in your presence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not aware of that, because when these documents were given I was no longer in the station for traffic security. I now hold a different post and have different duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: However, you recognise that third page as coming from the accounts department, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I assume on the basis of the numbers, the orderly numbers, the last number is 150 because I know that we did not have so many policemen in our station.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I tender this now to the Court as the next Defence Exhibit. I think some numbering has gone awry actually because I remember that at the end of Friday we had a video photo taken of the marked photograph by the witness of that date, and that would have been D74.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I recall that I had asked counsel to reach an agreement, put a mark on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I did not know that it was going to be introduced as another Exhibit. If it was given another number, I do not know, Mr. Bos, whether you would have known that?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: It has not been given a number.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: It was not given a number. Why do we not just make that 76 since it has not been given a number and that will be the photo with the marking by Witness B, was it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: So there is no objection to Defence 76. I gather there was an agreement made. That was Witness B who identified his sentry post? No objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: There is no objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK, Defence 76, that will be admitted. 74 has been marked for identification purposes but not offered. 75 now you wish to offer. Is there any objection to Defence 75? This is, what, the last one that this witness was talking about?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. At this time we are not satisfied this witness has authenticated this document. Perhaps we could in our cross-examination, if Defence does not, we could ask some additional questions, so perhaps we could withhold our decision whether to object or not object at this time?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. It is a several page document. How many pages is it, three?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It is three pages.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: It is the last page that really presented us a problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It is the last page.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Let us hold off and, if you want to, see what can be developed on cross-examination, or at this point, I do not know that this witness is able to testify as to where this document comes from except his belief that it would come from the accounting because of the orderly fashion ----

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: --- like all accountants and because of the number, 150. So there may be a foundation problem with the last page, but the first two pages ----

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The first two pages should go in, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: What was problem with the first page?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, my understanding of the testimony so far ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Let us ask. Mr. Prpos, would you please take off your earphones? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, my understanding of the testimony so far is that this witness was not present when these documents were provided to the Defence. This witness did not sign the first two pages even though his name is signed on those pages. There is no indication he prepared these documents. There is no indication these documents were in his keeping. So, I think at this point in time they have not laid the foundation to authenticate these documents through this witness.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: They form the usual category of almost business records of which he is able to support the authenticity because they are documents that arise in the course of the employment of the particular person, the accused, which bear his name and he is able to authenticate them in that form as being that category of document that arises from the nature of employment of the person who has his name on it.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We are now down to a business record exception to hearsay and I do not know how it would be done in your system, but you might need to have the custodian of the record to come and testify that (a) this is a record; that it was kept either by him or under his direction; that it was kept in the normal course of business. That is, kind of, my understanding. I do not know what it would be in my fellow Judges' jurisdiction. We do not even have a business record exception. We do not have a hearsay rule either. It is really, though, a question of foundation and authenticity. I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: May I say these are typed documents with a stamp on them and a signature.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: They look good.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. I am surprised at the objection really. (The learned Judges conferred).

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will suspend ruling on this offer of Defence 75 at the present time. We will give you an opportunity to cross-examine and perhaps you will be able to better -- you have articulated, but perhaps the Judges will understand -- I will understand better the basis for your objection. So we will reserve ruling on Defence 75 at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have copies here for you which I think will make it rather clearer to see what we are looking at. If eventually you reject the material, you can reject these, but I think it will make it easier.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Sure. At the present time, though, let us move forward and let us see whether we are going to admit them. So I will reserve ruling on 75 at the present time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can I turn you back to the first page of document ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Marro, would you ask Mr. Prpos to put his earphones on, please? Mr. Kay, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can I put you back to that first document labelled "C1" again, Mr. Prpos?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is that document headed amongst its heading the words "June 1992"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you tell us how this document comes to be compiled?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This document was compiled in the militia station for traffic security on the basis of records of work of policemen during a particular month, that is, throughout the month of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Does this document contain the name of Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, under No. 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Who would have filled in this record?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The typist who typed this out, but Zoran Cvijic is responsible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You referred to there being a signature on this document in that line of 12. Whose signature would that be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is most probably the signature of Dusko Tadic that he received this amount of money.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When would this document be presented to the policeman for signature?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When this amount of money is paid out to the said person. This is proof of having received the money.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The money that has been paid to the policemen, who calculates that sum?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is calculated by the person who works in the accountancy department of the public security station ----

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we look ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: --- and one can see that this was written out in writing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we look at the headings of the columns of this document, can you tell us what the headings are?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: First, the number, then the surname and name and then "engaged from, to", the number of days, the amount of dinars and then signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When would it say that Dusko Tadic was engaged from and to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You can see it there, from 16th until 30th June.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What does it say under the number of days?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The total number of days.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How many is that recorded as being?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It says 13.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Under whose authority is this document compiled by Zoran Cvijic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Under my authority, but then there is also the records that existed and also the schedule.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So the documents we have previously looked at, being the official duty plan and the schedule of hours worked, are the documents that are used to calculate the wages?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, those are the documents used.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Looking at this page here it has your name on it, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Where is that, Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The first part, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, typewritten.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Whose signature is that through your name and the station Commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the signature of Dusan Jankovic, the Assistant Head of Department for police affairs. I was probably away at the time and it was necessary to pay salaries to policemen, so he signed it in my name.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Are you familiar with this kind of document? Have you seen it before in Prijedor police station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, while I worked there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is it compiled properly and as you would expect such a document to be compiled?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In this specific case, it should be so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I would like you now to look at the next page. Do you recognise this copy document that is before you now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What is this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is also a list of the reserve members of the police force on the basis of which salaries were paid to the policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is it then the same kind of document as the one we have just been looking at?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Does it show at line 8 the name of Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Dusko Tadic under No. 8.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is there a signature in the right-hand column of the page?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there is a signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Who would sign at that part of the document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not tell. Basically, the person who took the amount concerned. It did not have to be Dusko Tadic personally; one of his colleagues could have picked it up for him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Does it show how much money he would have received during his working period?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In the bottom right-hand corner of the document is your name typed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That is Djuro Prpos. Is there a signature there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document as being a document that is part of the usual police records at Prijedor police station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, in view of the answers relating to the first two pages of this document, I would submit now that it is fully indicated sufficiently for the Court in terms of authentication.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: No objection to the first two pages, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. Defence 75, the first two pages, will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour noting the time as being 4.00, would that be an appropriate moment?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes. We will stand in recess for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Marro, we are ready to proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: He is not!

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Mr. Prpos, I would now like you to look at the third page of that document that was marked C1. Do you have that document now before you and is it headed with the figure "4" at the top of the page?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is the name Tadic Dusko in the column at point 128?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it says Dusko Tadic under No. 128.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is there again a signature on that page at the same line of 128?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, there is a signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you tell us then where this document comes from?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The English interpreter says the tone is intermittent. I cannot interpret this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I do not know whether there has been interference or not.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: See if Mr. Prpos can hear us? Mr. Prpos, can you hear us? No.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I always feel when we have this down time we should be doing something, so perhaps we will. The Defence will finish, you anticipate, on October 25th. The Prosecution wanted one week recess. That will be granted. Then the Prosecution had previously indicated that they will need about one week for rebuttal. So we would then begin with rebuttal, what is that week, the week of November 4th, or whatever that Monday is.

utterances.speaker: MISS FEATHERSTONE
utterances.text: Yes, Monday 4th.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: So if things go as they plan, then the Defence will finish October 25th or thereabouts. Then we will stand in recess for one week and then we will return and hear from the Prosecution in rebuttal.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We seem to be on-line.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Prpos, can you hear us? Very good. Thank you. Mr. Kay, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Mr. Prpos, if you could look at the third page then of that document C1 which has the No. 4 at the top of the page, can you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you tell us where this document comes from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the document from the accountancy department of the public security station.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Have you seen a document like this before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, when taking out salaries.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Who prepares this document within the accountancy department?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: It is intermittent again, the interpreter says, I cannot hear it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Who prepares this document within the accountancy department?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is prepared by the authorised worker who is in the accountancy department.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What information do they use to compile this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They use the previous list which comes from the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The signature in column 7, who would be supposed to sign at that point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It should be signed by the worker, the person to whom the mentioned amount pertains to, that is the salary, or somebody on his behalf if he was authorised to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is this document that is before you now compiled in the usual way for such documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Would the original page, in fact, have names on the rest of the numbered points?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Has this document been given in a form to the Defence that has been to take out the names of the other people who were on the original page?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It would be known by the person who gave this, that is to say, the worker from the accountancy department. I did not give this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But have the other names on the page been taken out as a condition of the Defence receiving this document?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Objection, your Honour. He has stated he was not present when the document was given. He did not give the document, so how does he know why it was taken out?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: It has been asked and answered. He has repeated it again, he did not give the document so he does not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I did wonder whether there has been a translation problem or some other difficulty in receiving this question, your Honour, because I am not asking about where it came from, but the fact that the other names have been taken off the page.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Does this form contain the period within which the police officer would have worked at Prijedor police station for the month of August?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in this specific case it is from the 1st to 31st August in the case of Dusko Tadic and the number of days too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Would that number of days be 26?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For the person who worked, yes, if the person worked for that long, so this paper gives the number of days.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this stage I renew my application for the document to be exhibited on the basis that there has been sufficient authenticity.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we believe that our objections will go to the weight of this document. We do not object based on authenticity.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes. We were going to admit it because it really goes to the weight. We have relaxed rules and I would like to let it in, to get as much as we possibly can in terms of relevant facts, and it appears to be relevant, that is for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, there are copies here for the Court.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is this going to be 77, is it? It originally was a part of 75, but we will make it a new exhibit, I guess.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: D77, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK, good. D77 will be admitted. MR. KAY (To the witness): That is all I ask about this particular document. Thank you, Mr. Prpos. What I would like to ask you about now is the control you, as the Commander of the traffic police, exercised over the policemen who worked underneath you. Did you make any checks upon your policemen at their various points of duty?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did that on a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We have been looking in the books and in the station register at the hours of duty for Dusko Tadic. Did you have any complaint against him as a police officer that he missed his duty or was absent from his post?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: While I carried out the control and while I was in the police station, I had no objections regarding his performance.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If one of your police officers turned up for his duty drunk, would you have tolerated that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What was the routine of the police officers at checkpoint Orlovci for reporting for their duty?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As a rule, they go on duty from the police station itself but, in view of the circumstances at the time, people went directly to their post. So that in view of the distance of the checkpoint, the policemen went there on their own and there was no regular transportation, but during their shifts I would come and control their work.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you know if there was a car available for the policemen at checkpoint Orlovci to be taken to their checkpoint to commence their duty?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It depended on circumstances. Sometimes there was a vehicle available to take the shift there and bring them back, but very often there was no such vehicle available, so they had to get there on their own one way or another.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Would the police officers report to the police station before starting their duty so that they were recorded as having been present for their shift?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If they were going to their shift from the station or if there was a vehicle available, yes, but if there was no possibility for transporting them there, they would go there directly. But I would check their presence on a daily basis to make sure that they were coming on time, and the leader of the shift had to prepare a report saying who was there, whether anyone was absent, and there is a report to cover each shift. Also, at the checkpoint a record was kept on a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions, but wait there, please.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis, cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Witness, could you please tell us your day and month of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: May 1st 1952, in a place called Lamovita, the opstina of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Are you known by any nicknames?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They call me "Duka".

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Could you tell us the address of your current residence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Prijedor, Mese Selimovica Street, C2.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How long have you lived there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For -- I did not get the beginning of the question.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How long have you lived at your current address?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have been living there since ----

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I am sorry. The interpreter did not get that, the year.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I am sorry, could you tell us again the year in which you first moved to that address?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you know who lived at that address prior to your living there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Mehmed Krajisnik, the former Commander who was my Commander too.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did that individual own the residence at that address?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was not the owner. He was a tenant because the apartment belongs to the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you know who previously owned that apartment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do, Krajisnik Mehmed, as I just said.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You indicated he was not the owner. Do you know who owned that apartment prior to the Ministry of the Interior taking it over?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the beginning, from the moment the building was erected, it belonged to the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How is it that you were able to get an apartment in that building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Upon the insistence of the former user, Krajisnik Mehmed, I exchanged with ----

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In what section of Prijedor is your address located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is a settlement called Pecani.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You indicated, I believe, that you have four children. Could you tell us the dates of birth of your children?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Could you tell us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Please do so. What are the dates of birth of your children?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The youngest was born on December 17th, 1995; the next was born on 14th June 1980 and the 24th June 1982, and the oldest is a child from my second wife's first marriage. He is Danijel, born in 1979.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you. What is your father's name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Vaskrsija.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Does he have any nicknames?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They call -- everybody calls him "Kiso".

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Prior to working for the police in the station in Prijedor, did you work for the police in Ljubija?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did from 1974 until 1979 and I lived there until 1984.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You have indicated that you continued to work for the Prijedor police department and that you are currently a Major and your position is you are the Inspector for the co-ordination and monitoring of traffic police, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How long have you held that particular position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This last position?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From 1994, in August.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: At this time who is your immediate superior?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dragan Stojicic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What is that person's official duty title?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He is head of the department for police affairs.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: At this time who is the Chief of Police in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know which police you have in mind.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Let me ask you, for some time, at least, Simo Drljaca was the Chief of Police in Prijedor. Does he continue in that position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When he was in that position, what was the scope of his authority? Was it for the entire opstina or only for the town of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Prijedor opstina.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who has taken his place? Who is now the Chief of Police for opstina Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. The post of deputy is being performed by Dusan Jankovic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The Chief of Police for opstina Prijedor, who does that person report to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You must ask him that.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You do not know what the official reporting is from the Chief of Police upward?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know what my responsibility is, but I do not know as regards the Chief of Police.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your immediate superior, does that superior report to the Chief of Police for opstina Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Most probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us when it was that Simo Drljaca relinquished his job as Chief of Police for opstina Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know exactly. I do not know the date but it was this year.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us when Simo Drljaca first took over as Chief of Police for opstina Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do, it was on 29th April 1992.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did he hold that post continuously until very recently?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mostly, more or less.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What time periods did he not hold that post, if you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In the spring of 1992, prior to the attacks on Hambarine and Kozarac and other Muslims villages, prior to those attacks, what was your position in the Prijedor police department?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was before the war deputy Commander of the traffic police, and the Commander was Fikret Kadiric until 29th April 1992. After that, I became the Commander of the traffic police station.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was Fikret Kadiric's ethnic group, if you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do know. He was Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: On 29th April 1992 and 30th April 1992, the Serbs took over the positions of authority in opstina Prijedor, did they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is so.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When did you first learn that the Serbs were going to take that action?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the eve of the 29th.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So prior to that you had no idea at all that this was going to happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not know.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How did you learn of that on the night of 29th April?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was called in.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who called you in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was called in by my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Which colleague was it who you called you in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My colleagues at work.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Tell us their names, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were quite a number of them.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: That is fine. Tell us the ones you remember.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All my colleagues who were working in the station with me.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Tell us the names of those you remember, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember any one of them just now.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You cannot remember any of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Not even one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not one.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: These were colleagues you worked with daily?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You had worked with these colleagues for years?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Until you were called in on the evening of 29th April you did not know that this Serb takeover was planned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not know because I never thought about it until the moment when at a common meeting we learned that the Territorial Defence of Bosnia and Herzegovina was preparing to block barracks because we had been together with the other workers who were Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who told you that that was going to happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: An official telegram arrived at the meeting and present was also the former head of department of the public security station, Hasan, the Commander, Fikret Kadiric, and representatives of parties, Mirzo Mujadzic and Simo Miskovic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who else was present at this meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For the moment I can just remember them and, of course, the other workers employed in the public security station.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So you cannot remember your other colleagues who were present at this meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Most of them were there, both Muslims and Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: But you cannot remember the names of any of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I cannot.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Is it not true, however, that a secret Serb police force had been created months before this event?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
