utterances.text: Is it not true that it was this secretly created Serb police force that was ready and took over on 29th and 30th April in opstina Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your question is not clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Is it not true that it was this secret Serb police force that was ready and in place and took over power on 29th and 30th April 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I told you that I did not know that there was any secret police force until the eve of 29th.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Prior to this takeover on 29th and 30th April 1992, you had frequent meetings with members of the JNA that were in Prijedor, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You did not meet with them frequently in your office at the police station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you know a man by the name -- I am sorry, sir. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Except for contacts that we had at a joint checkpoint which existed in Kozarac long before the war formed upon orders of the former Ministry of Internal Affairs headed by the Minister, Alija Deljimustovic(?). At that checkpoint, members of the military police were working. Those were the only contacts between the civil and military police that I was aware of.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When was that joint checkpoint created in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Long before the actual events. After the events in the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us what month and year it was created?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember exactly, but before the war there was this checkpoint in Kozarac while Fikret Kadiric was still the Commander.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How long did that joint checkpoint continue to exist in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It existed until the events that took place in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was in May. I do not recollect exactly the date, but it was in May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you say "until the events that took place in Kozarac", do you mean until the attack on Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know what attack you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You are not aware of any attack that occurred on Kozarac in May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but this came after events when a soldier was killed at Jakupovici on the road to Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So when you say that this joint checkpoint existed until the events that took place in Kozarac, you are talking about the attack on Kozarac, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What events are you talking about then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The events after the killing of a soldier on the road that I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What events? What do you mean by "events"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When the soldier was killed by Muslim extremists.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What action did the Serbs take after a soldier was killed? What did they do in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You do not know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was not au courant. I was responsible for the activities under my responsibility and not for military affairs.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: There were no civilian police at the joint checkpoint at Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were police from the traffic police station and the military police ----

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So those police from the traffic ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: --- they were.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Those police from the traffic police station would have fallen under your jurisdiction, would they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My jurisdiction and of Fikret Kadiric who was working at the time. I was his deputy at the time.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know a man by the name of Zoran Karlica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So, Zoran Karlica never visited your office in the spring of 1992 in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I believe you indicated that after the Serb takeover of Prijedor you became the Commander of the traffic police, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who promoted you to that position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The chief of the station.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Simo Drljaca.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did he personally tell you ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I just took over.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did he personally tell you that ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I just took over ----

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did he personally tell you that you had been promoted to the Commander of the traffic police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not personally. I gave the documents later. I just continued the duties I had performed as a deputy and I took over as Commander until I was appointed when by a decision of the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Srpska I was appointed to this post, but I was acting Commander until then.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who told you that you were acting Commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Simo Drljaca.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When did he tell you that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After the takeover of authority.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: That would be the next day after the takeover?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was implied. I just continued the work I had been doing before.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: This would have been the next day after the takeover that Simo Drljaca told you you were the acting Commander, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One may put it that way.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How long did you hold that position? I think we may have lost it. Witness, I will repeat the question that I had asked. How long did you hold the position of Commander of traffic police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Until 1994.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where was your office located, in what building, in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The headquarters of the station.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Is that a building sometimes people refer to as the SUP building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Have you ever been interviewed by any journalist, either Serb journalist or non-Serb journalist?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Have you ever given any ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: --- not as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Have you ever given any statements for any newspaper, magazine, television programme or radio programme?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean the overall preceding period?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter cannot hear him.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I am sorry. We could not hear that answer. Would you repeat the answer, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were professional statements in the domain of traffic exclusively local radio and television.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you make these statements before the conflict or after the conflict?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before the conflict.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Have you watched any of this trial on television?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, every now and then because time permitting really.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Which witnesses have you watched testify?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not a single one.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you watched ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I watched -- I did watch the witnesses of the Prosecution, yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you remember the names of any of those witnesses whose testimony you watched on television?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think I only remember a Mirsad Mujadzic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How often did you watch these proceedings on television?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Seldom, seldom, because I worked, so I could not follow it all the time.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where would you be when you would watch this trial on television? Would you be at home? Would you be at the police station? Where would you be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At home, at home when I get back home for work.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Has anyone ever told you not to watch this trial on television?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was told not to watch it when I found out that I would be a witness.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, when was that? When were you told?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember the date exactly. I remember when Mr. Kay was here, then I was told about that.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you remember what month that was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two or three months ago.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In the spring and summer of 1992, what type of vehicles did the police use in opstina Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They used vehicles with police plates and also civilian cars depending on the actual duty involved. We, in the traffic police, would use civilian vehicles when we were checking on speed limits, for example.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: These civilian vehicles, would they have any particular types of markings to identify them as police vehicles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were marked like any other police vehicle, that is, alarms and it also said "Police". It was written "Police".

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What colour were these civilian vehicles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Civilian vehicles, it depends, red, white, grey.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The regular police vehicles, what colour were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Blue and white, blue and -- there was white colour on the back and on the front, up front.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What type of vehicles were they, what manufacture of vehicle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the traffic police it was primarily Golfs, a few Jugos, Zastava 101 and the like.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Before the attacks began on Muslims villages in May 1992, prior to that time, how many traffic police officers were there in opstina Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Together with the Muslims there were about 30 all together.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: And after ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Together with the leadership, I mean.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So there would have been 30 total personnel in the traffic section of the opstina Prijedor police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, this is just the active personnel. The reserve personnel was much larger because it included Muslims too.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How many of these reserve personnel were performing duties with the traffic police prior to 22nd May 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Until after the takeover, there were reserve policemen who included Muslims but then after the takeover the Muslims left.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Before the takeover, how many reserve police total would there have been who were actually performing duty, that is, including both Serbs and non-Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were about 20 odd people altogether.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After the Serb takeover at the end of April 1992, how many Muslims continued to work in your section of the Prijedor police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: None of them remained. They all withdrew to Kozarac and Ljubija. They joined their own stations there and they worked there. There were certain attempts to persuade some of them to work there, but they did not agree to that because they would have to sign a solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What is this solemn declaration they would have to sign?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That they accept the laws of Republika Srpska and that they would enforce them. It is the usual kind of declaration that is made in police, like in any other police force.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you sign such a declaration after the Serb takeover of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did all of the police officers who worked for you sign such a declaration?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did all the Reserve Police officers who worked for you, who came to work for you in June, July and August 1992 also sign such a declaration?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During the months of June, July and August 1992 how many traffic policemen worked for you in opstina Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember the exact number now, but depending on the actual needs we drew on the reserve force of the police.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Well, what would be an average ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The number would change.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What would be the lowest number that would have worked for you during that period?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember specifically what the number was, but the number varied practically every day depending on the actual needs involved, and then we would draw on the reserve force because after the departure of the Muslims from the station it was normal that this had to be filled up.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was it filled up to the same number you had before? Were there more people working for you? Give us a general number, if you can?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, that number, about 50.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: This would include both active duty and reserve or just reserve?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The total number active duty and reserve.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Can you ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because ----

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Please go ahead and finish.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Reserve Police officers had the same authority as regular police officers after they were mobilized.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where were you assigning these police officers, in what locations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was mainly checkpoints.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where were these checkpoints located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Checkpoint Orlovci, Sana Raskovac, Sena Dolijna (?), etc., sometimes Gomjenica.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Is the village of -- Mr. Prpos, can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Is the village of Petrov Gaj located within opstina Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you have any traffic police who came from Petrov Gaj?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: It looks like the picture is not working, Mr. Prpos is in the same pose.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, do you wish to stop -- no, we have lost it.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: How much longer do you think you have for cross and redirect?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would think another 30 to 45 minutes perhaps. Your Honour, there is one thing I would ask, if we can get the picture back up, I am going to ask you to direct to this witness to provide the unredacted versions of the Defence Exhibit that have been discussed here today. So, if we could deal with that before we close this session.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. Well, it appears that they are not getting the sound anyway or the picture. If it looks like they are getting it I will ask the witness to take his earphones off. What is the request? He has already done it. I will ask him again. Mr. Prpos, would you please take your earphones off? Thank you. Yes, go ahead, Miss Hollis.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. During the course of direct examination the Defence referred to several documents and asked this witness questions about them. All of those documents are redacted to a greater or lesser degree. I believe those are Defence Exhibits 63, 64, 65, 66, 75 and 77. We would ask that you order this witness to produce the unredacted version of those Exhibits for use both in cross-examination with this witness and also for other possible cross-examination or rebuttal. Your Honour, I suggest that the reason that we would allowed these documents is, number one, they have been referred to by the Defence and under completeness we would ask to review the entire document. Secondly, the other names that appear on that document would be relevant to us both to test the accuracy and the completeness of these documents which this witness has told us are very complete. In addition to that, they would be relevant to determine what types of duties these other individuals were purportedly performing who are named on these documents. So we would ask that you order this witness to produce them.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Marro, we have asked Mr. Prpos to take off his earphones and we want to assure there is no Serbo-Croatian translation going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARRO
utterances.text: No problem, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: "No problem" means no, right? OK, thank you. Mr. Kay, what is your response now regarding the request for complete documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This request is not without its problems. We have had to extract these documents from Prijedor Police Station in the form that we have been given. What concerns me is that this may be a request that causes great difficulty for this trial and for this particular witness. He has made himself available to the -- well, he had made himself available to the Defence and I see an empty chair -- in the circumstances in which we are able to get these people to co-operate to the limited degree we can. I believe this Court knows a great deal from the evidence it has heard about the power of certain people in this particular region. They are not in positions that are easy and requests that are made that can put them into personal difficulty, particularly if they cannot be fulfilled, may have consequences for those witnesses. I am not using this in a form of aggression but almost like a intimidatory tactic against these individuals. What concerns me is that there can be consequences that can cause a witness and, indeed, this trial to have great problems. About that I can say no more. I think the Court appreciates we have obtained these documents and we have been into the police station to get them. We have done our best.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: What I hear as far as why the names were excised, listening to Mr. Prpos, was he said those were not relevant. The question becomes, well, who made the decision as to relevancy? That is the problem. When they are turned over to you and a decision is made by a person in power that, "This is all I am going to give you", then that raises a problem just in terms of our ability even to compel this individual to turn over more. Certainly I imagine in any system, or at least in any common law system, in terms of the completeness of a document that is something that is recognised. What that means is that one side should not be able to choose what it wants from a document and put the document in and then not let the other side see the entire document. I think that is a pretty universal concept that would be recognised. Is that not true, my fellow Judges? So the notion of completeness is not foreign and the rationale is simple. It is to be fair for both sides.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We have not made the decision on relevance. We have not told them to edit these documents. We were unable to see them until they were provided to us in this form. We have not asked for incomplete records to be put in this form before the Court.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Let me confer with my fellow Judges and see if they agree with me on my notion of completeness. Then of course there is a problem with just the production, whether we have the power even to do that. But there are questions I had about some of these documents and some names that I would be interested in. So it is going to affect how I might even look at these documents. (The Judges conferred).

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: My fellow Judges agree with my view on the notion of completeness, that is that if you offer part of a document then the other party can compel the entire document to be offered. The reason is obvious whether we are in common law or civil law I think. We want to have the complete document. The real power is our ability to compel. Judge Vohrah has suggested that there is no harm in asking the witness, directing him even, to produce the entire document. If he tells me, "Well, the powers that be made the decision that we would only give this", there is not too much I can tell him, I think, in terms of the power that this Tribunal has, unlike a national system.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, the Defence have no difficulty with the request. It is just that I am making a point to the Court about this as I do not want it reflected upon the Defence.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I understand. I hope that the witness is still there and I will ask that he return. Do you have anything else to add, Miss Hollis, at this point?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we understood they were given these in redacted form. That is why we ask you to make the request, the order of this witness. We would note, however, that we have been told that in fact at least one or more of the Defence team have seen the unredacted documents even though they could not copy them. But again that really is peripheral I think to the problem here.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. Have you seen the complete document?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, but I cannot say I have memorized it or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: It is Serbo-Croat and English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I insisted on seeing it so I knew what was being put before my eyes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The reasons that were given you for the redaction were?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It is a need-to-know basis as far as I am concerned.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Pardon me?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I was being treated on a need-to-know basis. I was being given only what I was going to receive.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: So did you ask for more and get only what you received?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, and I asked to make sure that I could see an authentic -- well, I will not give evidence, but I asked to see something so I knew where it came from.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I think it is appropriate since there was mention of the fact that a member of the Defence team had seen it. I do not think you are giving evidence out of sorts. Let us talk with Mr. Prpos. Mr. Marro, would you ask Mr. Prpos to put his earphones on, please. Mr. Prpos, this is Judge McDonald talking. Mr. Prpos, regarding certain Exhibits that you made reference to in your testimony, the Tribunal is requesting that you produce the complete copies of these Exhibits. The copies that we have been presented are only partial, in that certain names and other information is taken -- can you hear me still? Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can hear you. I can hear you. I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Certain information is taken out of these Exhibits. You referred to them when you said that information had been blanked out. The Tribunal is requesting that you produce these documents completely without the blanked out portions, and they are Exhibits 63 -- these are Defence Exhibits -- Defence Exhibit 63, 64, 65, 66, 75 and 77. Those are the documents that you made reference to today during your testimony. Are you able to produce those documents in their complete form without the blanked out portions or with the blanked out portions not being blanked out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I am concerned, because at present I am not in the Traffic Security police station, so all of that would be addressed to the present Commander of that station. So I do not have the authority now to give anything from those records because I am not authorised in that station now. These records remain in the station regardless of who is the Commander.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Who is the Commander again of the traffic police now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At present it is Mile Jankovic. I have testified on the basis of what I know in relation to the documents that were made while I was Commander of the police station.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis, is there anything else? Mr. Kay? Mile Jankovic I understand is the present Commander.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: He is the person who would have custody of these records?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I do not know how I could compel -- I was looking at the witness list and I do not see him as a witness for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: He is not, your Honour. He declined.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: So he is not a witness. What authority do I have to compel?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What actual authority you have to compel even with this witness I guess is a question, but I might suggest that you request of this witness to pass your request on to Mr. Jankovic and have a reply tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. Mr. Prpos, would you ask Mr. Jankovic if he will produce these documents in their complete form, the ones I referred to by Defence Exhibit numbers, so that you may bring them with you when you return tomorrow to complete your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can try, but I cannot guarantee because this is exclusively within his authority. But I believe that insight can be made in a different way in terms of authenticating these documents. I think the people who have been crossed out are not all that important. These are simply the names of other policemen who do not want to appear in this kind of case. There are numbers and it is obvious that this is an excerpt in which Dusko Tadic appears.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: This is a trial and both sides want access to the information. So, if you will pass on this request, please, to Mr. Jankovic, and the request is that he give to you the complete copies of those Exhibits that I referred to by number, that is Defence Exhibits 63, 64, 65, 66, 75 and 77, so that you may bring them with you tomorrow. You indicate to him that that is a request that has been made by the Tribunal. Would you do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I shall tell him, but as far as the outcome is concerned I cannot be the judge of that.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Prpos. You are now excused until tomorrow at 10 a.m. and we will resume the testimony then. The Court is adjourned until 10 a.m.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The court adjourned until the following day).

procedural_notes.text: (The Court adjourned for a short time)
(The Court adjourned for a short time)
